newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli shekel rises against dollar.
newsitem.headline: Israeli shekel rises against dollar.

text.p: The Israeli shekel's representative rate was fixed slightly higher against the dollar on Wednesday in quiet trading, dealers said.
"On Tuesday the shekel started rising against the dollar after the setting of the representative rate as the dollar weakened abroad," said Ilan Zadka at United Mizrahi Bank.
"On Wednesday trading was quiet and the shekel was stable, but the Bank of Israel had to intervene again in the market, buying dollars to support the basket," Zadka said.
Dealers estimated the central bank purchased $70 million to $100 million.
The central bank has been intervening regularly in the market to support the currency basket, which has been trading at the bottom end of its band for three months.

The representative rate for the dollar was fixed at 3.4070 shekels against 3.4100 on Tuesday. The basket, composed of the dollar, mark, pound sterling, French franc and yen, was fixed at 3.6788 shekels against 3.6785 on Tuesday.
On the crosses, the shekel traded against the yen at 2.6877 shekels per 100 yen compared with 2.6918 on Tuesday, and against the mark at 1.9726 shekels compared with 1.9690 on Tuesday.
In the late afternoon, the dollar was trading at 3.4060 shekels.
